children: Tanker freight rates have surged to historically high levels as restricted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz limits vessel availability six months into the Middle East conflict, S&P Global Energy says. Ship crossings through the waterway, which normally handles around 20% of global seaborne oil and LNG flows, have fallen by more than 80% since the U.S.-Iran war began on Feb. 28. The benchmark Middle East Gulf-Japan Long Range 2 tanker route hit an all-time high of $107.72 a metric ton on Aug. 27, according to Platts data. (farhan.rafid@wsj.com)
